name: Company Research Brief
description: Researches a named company on the web and produces a one-page, source-backed sales brief with company facts, recent news, and tailored discovery questions.

spec.name: Company Research Brief
spec.description: Researches a named company on the web and produces a one-page, source-backed sales brief with company facts, recent news, and tailored discovery questions.

company_name.description: Name of the company to research, optionally with a location or industry hint to disambiguate

our_product_context.description: Optional one-line description of what the sales rep is selling, used to tailor the discovery questions

confidence_notes.description: Notes on data gaps, ambiguity, or unverified facts

nodes.name: Input
nodes.description: Company name and optional sales context

nodes.name: Web research
nodes.description: Disambiguate the company, gather facts, profiles, and recent news with sources

config.system: You are a meticulous B2B research analyst. Never fabricate facts. If a fact (e.g. founding year, HQ) cannot be verified from a source you actually visited, record it as 'unverified'. If multiple companies match the name, pick the most prominent one and note the alternatives. Prefer primary sources: the company's official site, Wikipedia, Crunchbase, LinkedIn, and reputable press. Record the exact source URL and publication date for every news item.
config.task:
Research the company: {{input.company_name}}

1. Disambiguate the identity using any location/industry hint in the name; if several plausible matches exist, choose the most prominent and note the alternatives.
2. Find the official website and profiles (Wikipedia, Crunchbase, LinkedIn).
3. Determine: what the company does, founding year, headquarters location, and 3-5 key products or services.
4. Find at least 3 news items from the last 12 months (funding, leadership changes, product launches, partnerships, layoffs, earnings). Each item must have a title, publication date, and working source URL. Use current_time to know today's date.
5. Note any data gaps, ambiguity, or unverifiable facts.

Return a structured answer with: overview, founded, headquarters, key_products, news (title/date/url each), sources (url/title/accessed_date each), confidence_notes.

nodes.name: Normalize facts
nodes.description: Turn the research into clean typed fields, marking anything unverifiable

config.system: You normalize research notes into structured data. Do not invent or embellish any fact; if a field is missing or unverifiable, use the literal string 'unverified'. Keep source URLs exactly as given.
config.prompt:
Normalize this research into structured fields.

RESEARCH:
{{nodes.research.output.answer | json}}

Rules:
- overview: 1-2 neutral sentences on what the company does.
- founded: year or 'unverified'.
- headquarters: location or 'unverified'.
- key_products: 3-5 items.
- news: keep only items from the last 12 months, each with title, date, url; minimum 3 if available.
- sources: every URL cited, with title and accessed_date.
- confidence_notes: ambiguity in company identity, data gaps, unverifiable facts.

nodes.name: Draft discovery questions
nodes.description: Write three open-ended, company-specific discovery questions

config.system: You write sharp, specific B2B discovery questions. Each question must reference something concrete about the company (a product, a recent event, or its market) and must not be reusable verbatim for a different company. Open-ended, no marketing language.

nodes.name: Write the brief
nodes.description: Assemble the one-page markdown brief and enforce the quality bar

config.system: You write concise, neutral, factual sales briefs in markdown. Use only the provided information — never invent facts. Mark anything unverifiable as 'unverified'. No marketing language.
config.task:
Write a one-page markdown sales brief for the company using ONLY the data below.

COMPANY DATA:
{{nodes.extract_facts.output | json}}

DISCOVERY QUESTIONS:
{{nodes.draft_questions.output.text}}

Required sections in this order: ## Company Overview, ## Founded, ## Headquarters, ## Key Products/Services, ## Recent News (last 12 months), ## Three Smart Questions.
- Recent News: list each item as '- <title> (<date>) — <url>'.
- Keep the whole brief under 500 words excluding the sources.
- Neutral, factual tone; no marketing language.
- Use 'unverified' for any fact without a source.
criteria: The brief contains all six sections: Company Overview, Founded, Headquarters, Key Products/Services, Recent News, Three Smart Questions
The brief body is under 500 words
Every recent-news item includes a publication date and a source URL
No claim is presented as verified without a source or an 'unverified' caveat
Each of the three questions references something specific to this company and is open-ended
The tone is neutral and factual with no marketing language

nodes.name: Assemble output
nodes.description: Combine brief, sources, and confidence notes into the final result

nodes.name: Output
nodes.description: Final brief, sources, and confidence notes

plan.rationale: Open-ended web research with unpredictable steps (disambiguation, site discovery, news gathering) fits an autonomous agent node; a structured extraction step captures typed company facts; a refine loop enforces the explicit quality bar (six sections, ≤500 words, sourced news, neutral tone).

steps.purpose: Disambiguate the company (using the location/industry hint), find its official site and profiles (Wikipedia/Crunchbase/LinkedIn), gather what it does, founding year, HQ, 3-5 key products, and at least 3 news items from the last 12 months each with source URL and date. Note ambiguities and unverifiable facts instead of guessing. Uses web_search/fetch_url; outputSchema captures facts, news items, sources, and confidence notes.
Normalize the research into typed fields: overview, founded (or 'unverified'), headquarters (or 'unverified'), key_products[], news[{title, date, url}], sources[{url,title}], confidence_notes.
Draft three open-ended, company-specific discovery questions referencing its products/news/market, tailored to our_product_context if provided.

Assemble the one-page markdown brief with all six required sections, ≤500 words, every news item dated with a working URL, neutral tone, 'unverified' where facts lack sources. Criteria: all sections present, word limit, every news item has date+URL, no unsourced claims, questions are company-specific.
Combine brief text, sources list (with accessed_date), and confidence_notes into the final output object.

# Sales Brief: Stripe, Inc.

## Company Overview
Stripe, Inc. is an Irish-American private financial services and SaaS company that builds payment processing and economic infrastructure for internet businesses. It offers APIs and tools for online and in-person payments, billing, fraud prevention, treasury, issuing, and AI-era products such as agent payments and token billing. Valuation, funding status, and recent revenue figures are unverified.

## Founded
2009

## Headquarters
Dual headquarters: South San Francisco, California, U.S. and Dublin, Ireland

## Key Products/Services
- Payments (payment processing APIs, Checkout, Link)
- Billing & invoicing (including usage-based/token billing)
- Connect (marketplace/platform payments)
- Radar (fraud prevention)
- Treasury / Issuing / Terminal (banking-as-a-service, card issuing, in-person payments)

## Recent News (last 12 months)
- Stripe helps Muse, Meta's new personal AI agent, shop across the internet with Link (2026-09-08) — https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-helps-meta-muse-shop-with-link
- Stripe celebrates 10 years in Singapore by expanding its infrastructure for global businesses (2026-08-25) — https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-celebrates-10-years-in-singapore-by-expanding-its-infrastructure-for-global-businesses
- Stripe agrees to acquire OpenRouter to help businesses optimize token routing and usage (2026-08-19) — https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-agrees-to-acquire-openrouter
- Stripe named a Leader by Gartner for its Billing product for third consecutive year (2026-08-18) — https://stripe.com/newsroom/news
- Eileen O'Mara named vice chair of Stripe; Tyler Bryson appointed chief revenue officer (2026-06-22) — https://stripe.com/newsroom/news

Note: the leadership-change item is verified only via the newsroom index listing, not the individual press-release page.

## Three Smart Questions
1. With the OpenRouter acquisition announced in August 2026, how are you thinking about integrating token routing and usage metering into Billing without disrupting the metered-billing workflows your Gartner-recognized Billing customers already rely on?
2. Since the Muse launch showed agents transacting through Link at scale, what's your current framework for deciding which agent-commerce merchants get early access, and how do you evaluate fraud exposure in Radar when the buyer is an agent rather than a human?
3. As you expand the Singapore infrastructure for businesses moving money across APAC corridors, where do you still see gaps in Treasury and Issuing coverage that force multi-processor setups for your global merchants?

---

**Sources:** Wikipedia (accessed 2026-09-27); stripe.com (accessed 2026-09-27); Stripe Newsroom (accessed 2026-09-27); OpenRouter acquisition press release (accessed 2026-09-27); Meta Muse/Link press release (accessed 2026-09-27).
